Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
abstract: <jats:p>Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.</jats:p>

Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored.
Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes.
Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement.
Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization.
Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.</jats:p>

title: HYBRID NETWORK INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM BASED ON SIGNATURE ANALYSIS AND MACHINE LEARNING METHODS
abstract: <jats:p>In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.</jats:p>

abstract: IntroductionCardiovascular (CV) disease is extremely common across the United States and is a leading cause of death among adults (18 years or older). However, not every adult in the United States has equal access to hospitals capable of cardiothoracic (CT) surgery and procedures such as coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Furthermore, certain regions of the United States have different numbers of individuals without reasonable access to CT surgery.MethodsThis article conducts an analysis of CT surgery accessibility using Quantum Geographic Information Systems (QGIS) software. Drive-time isochrone polygons were generated, representing the areas that can be reached within 60 min of hospitals capable of CT surgery. The hospitals included in this mapping are registered with the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) and confirmed by Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) codes as hospitals that perform at least CABG procedures. Decennial census population data overlaid with the drive-time polygons offers the percentage of adults with limited access to CT surgery.Results87.8% of the adult population of the United States lives within a 60-min drive-time of a CT surgery-capable hospital, with 12.2% outside of that threshold.ConclusionSubdivisions of the United States with a more urbanized population have better CT surgery coverage for adults. Adults aged 55-74 have slightly worse access to CT surgery than adults of other age groups.

title: Whole-Body Nuclear Medicine Imaging of Infection and Inflammation.
abstract: Nuclear medicine has a long-standing role in imaging of infection and inflammation because a single radiotracer administration can survey multiple organ systems and detect pathophysiologic abnormalities that may precede changes on anatomic imaging. Whole-body acquisition can localize an occult source of systemic illness, define the extent of infection beyond a known primary site, including septic emboli and metastatic foci, and map the distribution and activity of multisystem inflammatory disease for treatment planning and response assessment. This review examines whole-body scintigraphy, SPECT/CT, PET/CT, and PET/MRI, with emphasis on indication-specific protocols, field-of-view selection, and incremental diagnostic value. We discuss settings in which regional or dedicated acquisitions are appropriate, which are often obtained in addition to whole-body imaging. We highlight representative clinical applications including peripheral and spinal osteomyelitis, fever of unknown origin, cardiovascular infection, large-vessel vasculitis, and sarcoidosis. We also note the limitations of nuclear medicine imaging and the need to correlate it with clinical parameters and, when available, to compare it with anatomic imaging modalities. Lastly, we will provide insight into future directions in the field, including increasing incorporation of long-axial-field-of-view PET, emerging new radiotracers, and the use of artificial intelligence.

title: Multimodal Single-Cell Analysis Reveals the Prognostic Role of Myeloid Subpopulation-Associated PI3K/AKT Signaling in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) represents a major global health burden with rising incidence, marked heterogeneity, and poor prognosis, necessitating reliable biomarkers for prognostic stratification. This study conducted a comprehensive multi-omics analysis, combining a large amount of RNA-seq data from TCGA-LIHC with a single-cell RNA-seq database. Feature extraction using autoencoders and 12 machine learning algorithms was applied to identify prognostic biomarkers, followed by survival analysis, single-cell atlas construction, and experimental validation. Using multi-gene representations from autoencoders, the authors determined that the PI3K/AKT pathway is a critical survival-related pathway. Integrated single-cell analysis uncovered 12 distinct cellular clusters, with the myeloid subpopulation showing pronounced transcriptional dysregulation driven by PI3K/AKT signaling. The intersection of 2,567 upregulated genes from myeloid cells and 105 PI3K/AKT pathway-related genes identified 24 overlapping candidates. LASSO optimization yielded a robust predictive model (ROC-AUC = 0.949), consistently identifying RAC1 and SLC2A1 as core prognostic genes validated in the external cohort GSE76427. Both genes showed strong associations with adverse survival outcomes and EMT pathway activation. Western blot experiments confirmed that RAC1 and SLC2A1 knockdown modulate PI3K/AKT pathway activity, while transwell assays demonstrated suppressed migration and invasion. This study establishes a comprehensive framework integrating multi-omics profiling, single-cell transcriptomics, and machine learning to dissect HCC molecular heterogeneity. This study identified the PI3K/AKT signaling axis as a key prognostic driver in tumor-associated bone marrow subgroups and identified candidate biomarkers RAC1 and SLC2A1, providing mechanistic insights for the development of targeted therapies for this challenging malignant tumor.

title: Classifying mammogram images: combining Smooth Support Vector Machine (SSVM) and zoning feature extraction method.
abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide, making early and accurate diagnosis essential.. Mammography is widely used for breast cancer screening; however, distinguishing benign and malignant lesions remains a challenging due to subtle visual differences. . This study proposes a mammogram classification approach combining Smooth Support Vector Machine (SSVM) with zoning-based feature extraction. The framework consists of three main stages: image preprocessing, zoning-based feature extraction, and SSVM classification. Experiments were conducted using 322 mammogram images from the Mammographic Image Analysis Society (MIAS) database, comprising 207 benign and 115 malignant cases. Zoning was applied to extract regional intensity features, which served as input to the SSVM classifier. Experimental results achieved 97.50% training accuracy and 65% testing accuracy. The findings indicate that integrating zoning feature extraction and SSVM can capture relevant mammogram characteristics for breast cancer classification. However, the lower testing accuracy suggests potential limitations related to dataset size and feature representation. Future work will focus on integrating deep learning-based feature extraction to improve classification robustness and generalisation performance.

title: Artificial intelligence-based cephalometric analysis in unilateral and bilateral cleft lip and palate.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the agreement between 3 artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted automated and semiautomated cephalometric tracing programs and a clinical reference method (CRM) in the analysis of lateral cephalometric radiographs obtained from patients with unilateral and bilateral cleft lip and palate (CLP). Lateral cephalometric radiographs obtained from 67 patients (43 unilateral and 24 bilateral CLP) were calibrated and analyzed using NemoCeph (version 24.0.0.3; Nemotec, Madrid, Spain), WebCeph (version 1.5.0; Assemblecircle, Gyeonggi-do, Korea), and AudaxCeph (version 6.7.10.4983; Audax d.o.o., Ljubljana, Slovenia) to obtain 22 measurements. The CRM was the mean of independent digital manual tracings performed by 2 orthodontists. Interobserver reliability and direct AI-CRM agreement were assessed using 2-way mixed-effects, absolute-agreement, single-measure intraclass correlation coefficients [ICC (A,1)], and Bland-Altman analyses. Cleft-type effects were examined secondarily using generalized estimating equations with adjustment for multiplicity. CRM interobserver reliability was good or excellent for 20 of 22 measurements; U1-PP and the nasolabial angle showed moderate reliability (ICC range, 0.559-0.984). Direct AI-CRM agreement varied across the measurements and platforms, and the platform with the highest ICC differed according to the measurement being evaluated. All platforms achieved good or excellent agreement for several skeletal and vertical measurements, whereas Nper-A showed moderate overall agreement, and SN-PP showed poor agreement across all platforms (ICC, 0.278-0.389). Maxillary-incisor measurements most frequently showed low agreement. Bland-Altman analyses revealed wide or magnitude-dependent limits of agreement for several measurements, indicating that small mean biases did not imply individual-level interchangeability. Of 22 cleft-type-by-platform interactions, 9 remained significant after false-discovery-rate adjustment (q < 0.05). The direction and magnitude of these differences varied across the measurements and platforms, indicating no consistent group-related agreement pattern. The AI-CRM agreement varied across the measurements and platforms, with good agreement for most sagittal and vertical skeletal measurements, moderate overall agreement for Nper-A, and poor agreement for SN-PP across all the platforms. Lower agreement was observed for measurements involving CLP-affected dental structures and the nasolabial angle. For the nasolabial angle, substantial interobserver disagreement in the CRM limits the attribution of the discrepancy solely to AI performance. These programs may support cephalometric assessment in patients with CLP; however, verification by a clinician remains necessary.

title: A Seal Whisker-Inspired Optical Flow Sensor Array for Vortex Source Tracking.
abstract: Flow sensors endow underwater robots with 'hydrodynamic imaging' capabilities, facilitating exploration in complex aquatic environments, such as tracking ubiquitous vortex sources. However, existing underwater flow sensors suffer from low resolution and cannot independently extract critical parameters related to vortex sources, severely limiting practical applicability. Here, inspired by harbor seal whiskers, we report a highly sensitive bionic optical flow sensor (BOFS) array for high-precision vortex source tracking. The array integrates a single optical fiber with multi-point fiber Bragg gratings into x-shaped beams, enabling biaxial detection of flow signals along the major and minor axes. Experimental results demonstrate that the fabricated BOFS array achieves high-precision hydrodynamic perception, featuring a low flow velocity detection threshold of 7.4 mm s

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Optimization of Grounding Systems for 400 V, 10 kV, and 35 kV Electrical Installations: A Comparative Study.
abstract: This paper presents a novel AI-enabled optimization of grounding systems for 400 V, 10 kV, and 35 kV electrical installations. Grounding systems are important components of electrical power installations, equipment protection, and reliable operation under different fault conditions. Conventional grounding systems are generally limited by nonlinear soil characteristics, environmental discrepancies, and complex fault conditions. To address such challenges, a hybrid AI framework is proposed that integrates Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) into a unified intelligent platform to predict grounding resistance, diagnose faults, and perform multi-objective optimization. The ANN-LSTM method is employed to capture the nonlinear and temporal relationships in grounding parameters, whereas PSO is applied for multi-objective optimization of the grounding system. The proposed ANN-LSTM-PSO framework achieves prediction accuracies of 97.75%, 98.25%, and 98.75% for 400 V, 10 kV, and 35 kV systems, respectively. The experimental studies validate that the model minimizes grounding resistance and voltages under different soil and environmental conditions. This method also reduces grounding resistance, step, and touch voltages under different soil and environmental conditions. The developed Artificial Intelligence-Based Grounding Systems have been tested in residential infrastructure, such as residential complexes/apartments.

title: Evaluating Emotional Perception and Human Comfort in Urban Green Spaces Through Tree Diversity: A GIS and Survey-Based Approach.
abstract: This study investigates how tree diversity in urban green spaces influences emotional perception and human comfort, using survey-based perceptual data and spatial-ecological metrics. An online, map-based survey of 302 participants in Karlsruhe, Germany, was used to assess emotional comfort and perceptions of urban green space characteristics. Tree diversity was evaluated using multispectral satellite imagery and machine-learning-based classification, while spatial analysis was used to examine relationships between ecological characteristics and emotional responses. Perceived tree diversity was positively associated with emotional comfort (τ = 0.18, p < 0.001). Areas with greater tree canopy cover and mature trees were also associated with higher levels of human comfort and well-being. Gender and environmental education moderated perceptions of tree diversity, with female participants and participants with greater environmental knowledge reporting higher emotional comfort. Poorly maintained green spaces were negatively associated with emotional responses. Objective tree diversity, measured using the Shannon Diversity Index, showed non-significant associations with emotional responses (p = 0.58 and p = 0.12), highlighting a contrast between perceived and objectively measured biodiversity. The findings demonstrate that perceived biodiversity may be more relevant to emotional comfort than objective biodiversity measures and provide practical insights for the planning and management of urban green spaces.

title: AI-integrated versus Standard Mammography Screening Pathways: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Diagnostic Accuracy.
abstract: Purpose To compare the diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI)-integrated and standard mammography screening pathways for breast cancer detection using Bayesian network meta-analysis. Materials and Methods This prospectively registered review searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science through March 20, 2026, for diagnostic accuracy studies comparing two or more human-only or AI-integrated screening pathways using digital mammography or tomosynthesis. Bayesian bivariate random-effects network meta-analyses were fitted to a primary four-node and a secondary six-node network; risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 3 (QUADAS-3) and QUADAS-C tools, and certainty was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. Results Thirty-eight studies, with more than 4.2 million examinations, were included. In the primary digital mammography network (15 studies), AI as an independent reader (sensitivity, 78.9%; specificity, 95.8%) performed similarly to double human reading (sensitivity, 77.7%; specificity, 96.2%). title: Interpretable and Accurate Hybrid Decision Trees with Selective Case-Based Splits
abstract: Decision trees are among the most well-known interpretable models in Machine Learning. Over the years, a wide variety of strategies have been proposed to define split conditions within the greedy learning framework, aiming to guide instance routing and enhance predictive performance. These strategies range from axis-parallel and oblique splits based on feature values to proximity-based splits using exemplar instances and more complex hybrid approaches. However, no single method has emerged as universally superior. In this work, we present two key contributions to the construction of greedy decision trees. First, we propose a hybrid tree architecture that integrates both feature-based and case-based splits, allowing for heterogeneous splits throughout the tree. Second, we introduce a novel type of split that leverages a selective case-based approach: when a split is needed, our method searches for the most informative subset of features to define the split, effectively balancing the specificity of case-based methods with the simplicity of feature-based ones. Experiments on a diverse set of tabular datasets show that our method outperforms standard decision trees and achieves performance on par with ensemble methods, while producing shallow trees that retain or even improve predictive accuracy.
ai_summary: Decision trees are among the most well-known interpretable models in Machine Learning . They have been proposed to define split conditions within the greedy learning framework . They aim to guide instance routing and enhance predictive performance .

title: ProbFaS: Probabilistic Video Frame Selection for MLLMs via Multi-Fidelity Calibration
abstract: Processing long videos with multimodal large language models (MLLMs) is prohibitively expensive, making informative frame selection essential for accurate video understanding. The default uniform sampling often misses task-relevant keyframes, while recent training-free selectors instead pick frames by how well each one matches the question under an image-text alignment (ITA) score. However, we show that ITA signals correspond poorly with the MLLM's true needs: their rankings correlate weakly with downstream accuracy and are even negatively correlated on over 40% of questions, whereas the MLLM's internal yes/no judgment yields a much stronger signal. We present ProbFaS, a training- and label-free probabilistic pipeline that fuses both signals for key frame selection. ProbFaS treats dense ITA scores as cheap, biased measurements and sparse MLLM judgments as accurate, costly ones, unifying them via co-kriging, a multi-fidelity Gaussian process, to calibrate relevance across all frames. A temporal determinantal point process then selects frames capturing relevance peaks while preserving temporal coverage. Across Video-MME, MLVU and LongVideoBench, ProbFaS is the most accurate among fourteen state-of-the-art training-free selectors and uniform sampling in 13 of 15 settings (8-128 frames), outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 3.1 percentage points. On MLVU and LongVideoBench, 32 ProbFaS frames match or surpass the top baseline at 128 frames and uniform sampling with up to 768 frames.
ai_summary: The default uniform sampling often misses task-relevant keyframes . Recent training-free selectors instead pick frames by how well each one matches the question under an image-text alignment (ITA) score . We present ProbFaS, a training- and label-free probabilistic pipeline that fuses both signals for key frame selection .

title: Sliding-Window Detection of Hidden Regimes under Stochastic Switching
abstract: A sliding-window average is a simple estimator of the current state of a hidden regime-switching process, such as a hidden Markov model. A longer window averages out more noise but is more likely to contain a switch, and the question is what such a switch costs. We analyse the decoder that assigns the average of the last $m$ observations to the nearest regime mean. For two regimes with conditionally independent, stochastically ordered observations, a switch inside the window, averaged uniformly over its positions and directions, causes an error with probability exactly $1/2$. Consequently, for every stationary switching law, the error is at most $\bar P(m)+\bar s(m-1)/2$, where $\bar P(m)$ is the stationary-weighted single-regime error and $\bar s$ the switch rate. Under Markov switching, time reversal shows that a window whose oldest and current regimes differ is misclassified with probability exactly $1/2$, however many switches it contains, and the bound is attained up to a factor $p_{\min}^{m-1}$. For Gaussian noise with common variance, minimizing the bound gives an explicit window length which, in units of $σ^2/Δ^2$, depends only on the expected number of switches in that time. As switching probabilities vanish proportionally, the optimal error is $\bar s\log(1/\bar s)/(2I)(1+o(1))$, with $I$ the single-regime Chernoff exponent. In the Gaussian case this is twice the Bayes error. For symmetric switching, exponentially weighted moving averages reduce this factor to at most $2\log2\approx1.39$, and two-block weights adapted to the switch rate attain the Bayes rate. For three or more regimes, long-window switch costs are set by the geometry of the regime means. For Markov-modulated random walks with $\pm1$ steps on a reflecting lattice, a position-aware decoder learns as fast as without walls under holding boundaries, while steps at bouncing boundaries carry none.
ai_summary: A longer window averages out more noise but is more likely to contain a switch . We analyse the decoder that assigns the average of the last $m$ observations to the nearest regime mean . A switch inside the window, averaged uniformly over its positions and directions, causes an error with probability exactly $1/2$.

title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
abstract: Deep research agents gather information from multiple sources and synthesize it into reports on complex, open-ended questions. Existing benchmarks assess report quality along several dimensions, but lack a dedicated knowledge-centric evaluation of which research directions a report covers and how deeply it explores them. We introduce DRBench Pro, a benchmark that makes structured knowledge coverage the primary evaluation target. Our automated pipeline builds local knowledge trees from Wikipedia and uses sampled subgraphs to generate research queries and evidence-grounded rubrics. Each rubric corresponds to a relation in the tree, preserving the structure of the knowledge being evaluated. Agents receive only the research query. This structure allows us to measure breadth across major research directions and depth along related knowledge chains, with their geometric mean giving overall coverage. The benchmark includes 144 cases across 24 domains and 44,102 rubrics. Evaluating 16 deep research agents reveals different strengths in breadth and depth, with the best-performing agent reaching 57.04% overall coverage. Rubric judgments agree closely with human annotations, and agent rankings remain stable across the tested metric configurations.
ai_summary: DRBench Pro is a benchmark that makes structured knowledge coverage the primary evaluation target . The benchmark includes 144 cases across 24 domains and 44,102 rubrics . The structure allows us to measure breadth across major research directions .

title: A Survey of Security, Privacy, and Ethics of Large Language Models in Telecom
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into telecommunications for customer service, network analytics, and operational support. While offering efficiency and innovation, their deployment raises critical privacy, security, and ethical challenges due to the uniquely sensitive and longitudinal nature of telecom data. This paper presents a survey of LLM risks and safeguards in telecom context. Our survey introduces a telecom-specific taxonomy linking privacy, security, and ethics with use cases and outlines open research challenges such as longitudinal data privacy, cross-border compliance, and scalable guardrails.
ai_summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into telecommunications for customer service, network analytics, and operational support . This paper presents a survey of LLM risks and safeguards in telecom context . The survey introduces a telecom-specific taxonomy linking privacy, security, and ethics with use cases .

title: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
abstract: Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval. While such benchmarks measure how useful a model is, they provide no insight into the biology it represents. We introduce BioScore, a benchmark that quantifies how well an image encoder captures cell identities, with spatial transcriptomics of the same tissue as the reference. A sparse autoencoder splits the encoder's patch embeddings into sparse features, which we cluster into a fixed number of groups. BioScore then measures, for each of 52 cell identities defined by marker genes, how specifically one group follows the identity's expression over the tissue. Because the autoencoder training is fully unsupervised, a match shows that the model represents the cell identity from the image alone. We score 8 pathology foundation models and 3 natural-image models. Every pathology model scores above every natural-image model (0.299--0.371 \vs 0.214--0.232), and paired tests separate three tiers among the pathology models. Unlike a supervised probe, BioScore needs no labels, builds its reference from the data and scores even from few sections, yet it ranks the encoders as a probe does. Its per-identity breakdown indicates which cell identities each encoder captures or misses.
ai_summary: Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval . We introduce BioScore, a benchmark that quantifies how well an image encoder captures cell identities .

title: Proverbs As A Window On Collective Prescriptions
abstract: Proverbs, as repositories of traditional wisdom, have informed human reasoning for millennia. Yet the collective prescriptions they encode have remained largely unquantified. We introduce a computational framework to analyze nearly 50,000 English-language proverbs. Using large language models, validated against human judgments, we map the topical landscape of proverbs, assess their prescriptive power, and quantify their recommendations on key dimensions of human judgment and behavior. We find that most proverbs are prescriptive, offering guidance in domains under individual control, such as preparation and prudent action, whereas proverbs about uncontrollable circumstances, such as fate and mortality, tend to describe rather than prescribe. When prescriptive proverbs take a consistent stance, they favor caution over risk, long-term over short-term outcomes, honesty over deception, and kindness over malice, and show a moderate tendency toward suspicion over trust. On dimensions involving genuine trade-offs, especially autonomy versus compliance, proverbs provide contradicting advice rather than a single recommendation. This analysis provides a quantitative map of the collective prescriptions in a culture's proverbial wisdom, revealing a core of prudent, honest, and forward-looking guidance alongside varied advice where circumstances dictate the best course of action.
ai_summary: Proverbs are prescriptive, offering guidance in domains under individual control . Proverbs about uncontrollable circumstances, such as fate and mortality, tend to describe rather than prescribe . They favor caution over risk, long-term over short-term outcomes, honesty over deception .

title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
abstract: Looped Transformers boost expressivity by reusing shared layers across loops, yet at the cost of efficiency. Pushing their expressivity-efficiency frontier requires rethinking the core mechanism connecting adjacent loops: What should be passed as a Transformer loops? We introduce Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), whose Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA) uses keys and values (KV) as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops. Under loop residual, MoLT-R retains the residual stream and reads local KV across loops for expressivity. Under loop KV, MoLT-KV instead restarts from embeddings and reads current-loop local KV with preceding-loop memory KV at earlier positions for efficiency. MoLT-KV eliminates same-position cross-loop dependence and, paired with loop forcing for parallel training, unlocks single-traversal Mixture-of-Loops (MoL) decoding beyond the training loop horizon. To balance efficiency and quality, we introduce U-shaped MoLT (U-MoLT), which separates memory construction from prediction readout and skips unused decoder traversals without changing predictions. In 400B-token pretraining, U-MoLT outperforms OLMo3 across 700M/1.5B dense and 3B MoE models, achieving 1.7x validation cross-entropy (CE) token efficiency at 700M while improving 3B MoE 10-domain perplexity by 0.75 and 10-task accuracy by 2.1 percentage points. In 100B-token continued pretraining of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, our U-MoLT adaptation lowers CE on all 11 domains over the matched baseline with 1.4x mean token efficiency. At inference, U-MoLT with MoL-Hybrid-2 matches non-looped OLMo3 latency at 996.6 vs. 1,000.6 ms on S-size (~113M) models. Code is available at https://github.com/hustvl/MoLT

title: Repairing the Trustworthiness of Distilled Language Models
abstract: Knowledge distillation enables the deployment of large language models through smaller student models, but the compression process can introduce regressions in trustworthiness even when downstream performance is preserved. Repairing such failures is challenging because the original distillation corpus is often unavailable, while direct preference optimization may alter capabilities inherited from the teacher. We propose a targeted repair framework based on the proximal Bregman response function (PBRF) that addresses both limitations. We estimate the curvature required for PBRF using a surrogate proxy dataset, removing dependence on the original transfer corpus, and extend the framework to preference-based supervision through an odds-ratio objective. This enables the use of preferred and dispreferred response pairs while constraining changes to the distilled model. Our results show that the proposed approach improves targeted trustworthiness behaviors for both pre-training and post-training models while largely preserving downstream performance, providing a practical alternative to re-distillation or unconstrained preference optimization. Our experiment results show that across different distilled models, the trustworthy regression can be improved by up to 8% with less than 1% decrement in perplexity.
ai_summary: Knowledge distillation enables the deployment of large language models through smaller student models . But compression process can introduce regressions in trustworthiness even when downstream performance is preserved . Repairing such failures is challenging because the original distillation corpus is often unavailable .

title: AnyCam: Anything Can Represent Camera for Video Generation
abstract: Camera-controlled video generation re-renders a video along a target camera trajectory, yet moving the camera around an object, the most natural way to change the viewpoint of an object-centric scene, remains difficult. Existing methods condition either on camera parameters, which are scale-ambiguous in monocular video, or on explicit geometry such as warped point clouds or depth, which breaks down under large viewpoint changes. We present AnyCam, a method that represents the camera with an anchor object in the scene: we reconstruct it in 3D and render it along the target trajectory, a camera signal that is scale-aware, view-complete and easy to specify relative to the object. A video diffusion model transfers the content and dynamics of the source video to the new viewpoint. Its H-Concat layout aligns source and target frames in time, so the model can be distilled into AnyCam-AR, a streaming few-step generator for on-the-fly camera control. Both models are trained on paired videos with pixel-aligned anchor renderings from multi-camera videos and static-scene captures. Experiments on diverse datasets and trajectories show that AnyCam performs favorably against camera-controlled video generation and 3D reconstruction methods in camera control and visual quality.
ai_summary: Camera-controlled video generation re-renders a video along a target camera trajectory . Existing methods condition either on camera parameters, which are scale-ambiguous in monocular video, or on explicit geometry such as warped point clouds .

title: Full Structure Recovery of Linearized Reed-Solomon Codes
abstract: Linearized Reed-Solomon codes (LRS) are optimal sum-rank-metric codes that generalize both Reed-Solomon and Gabidulin codes, and benefit from excellent decoding capabilities, making them potentially interesting candidates for post-quantum code-based cryptography. Previous works have investigated the underlying geometric structure of LRS codes, identifying geometric invariants that distinguish them from random codes. Other works have proposed approaches to recovering the LRS structure from an arbitrary generator matrix, together with additional data. However, both the distinguishers and the recovery techniques proposed so far are either not fully general, or have a prohibitive computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a polynomial-time procedure for the full structure recovery of LRS codes from the sole knowledge of an arbitrary generator matrix. Our results show that, like their Hamming and rank metric counterparts, LRS codes cannot be used as they are for McEliece-like encryption. Our approach combines Overbeck-type attacks with suitable matrix manipulations and shortening techniques to recover the evaluation parameters across different ranges of code dimensions.
ai_summary: Linearized Reed-Solomon codes (LRS) are optimal sum-rank-metric codes that generalize both Reed- Solomon and Gabidulin codes . They benefit from excellent decoding capabilities, making them potentially interesting candidates for post-quantum code-based cryptography .

title: Spectrum Adaptation of AI-Native Autoencoder Communications with Transfer Learning
abstract: End-to-end physical-layer learning replaces separate modulation, coding, and detection operations with an autoencoder (AE) that consists of a jointly trained encoder-decoder pair at the transmitter and the receiver. This paper studies AI-native communications with AEs and quantifies the sensitivity to training-test mismatch in channel models. Models trained only on an AWGN channel achieve low bit error rates (BERs) under matched conditions but degrade severely on Rayleigh fading with practical front-end impairments. To reduce the time and energy required to adapt to new channel conditions, we propose a low-latency transfer-learning procedure that starts from an AWGN-pretrained system and fine-tunes only a small subset of transmitter and receiver layers while freezing the remainder. We further formulate layer selection as a budget-constrained optimization problem that identifies the most informative parameters to update during adaptation. This preserves the learned signal geometry and the deep decision structure while adapting lightweight front ends to fading- and impairment-induced mixing. For AE communications, we show that partial updates remove the mismatch-induced error floor and approach the BER of fully retrained models. We provide a layer-wise study and quantify resource-performance trade-offs, showing that modest adaptation substantially reduces BER while cutting training time, multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations, energy consumption, and the fraction of updated parameters for resource-efficient implementation.
ai_summary: The paper studies AI-native communications with AEs and quantifies the sensitivity to training-test mismatch in channel models . Models trained only on an AWGN channel achieve low bit error rates (BERs) under matched conditions but degrade severely on Rayleigh fading .

title: Tokenisation is not in APX
abstract: In this paper, we prove that, unless P=NP, no polynomial-time algorithm can find a tokeniser whose objective is within any constant factor of the optimum, meaning that tokenisation is not in the APX complexity class. We prove this for direct and bottom-up tokenisation, under both a compression or unigram log-likelihood objectives, and for binary or larger alphabets. We further show that, even over unary alphabets, direct tokenisation is APX-hard, and thus admits no polynomial-time approximation scheme.

title: Not all world models can doubt: how training objective and architecture shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models
abstract: World models predict how an environment responds to actions, so that candidate actions can be evaluated before execution. Executed actions, or decisions, taken in this manner are only as reliable as the model's predictive capabilities, and predictions in turn are only reliable within the model's experience. Epistemic uncertainty (EU) is the signal that marks where that experience ends. In this work we offer an extensive empirical study on how training objectives and architectures shape epistemic uncertainty of world models. More precisely, we present a controlled comparison of post-hoc EU (last-layer Laplace and ensembles) between two dominant models of different paradigms: 1) LeWorldModel (LeWM): A joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), which predicts the next embedding without a decoder, and 2) DreamerV3: A recurrent state-space model (RSSM), which reconstructs the observation from a recurrent latent state. In ten simulated visual-control environments, we follow a controlled state perturbation of the environment state through every stage of the models up to the final EU estimate. We find that the RSSM attenuates the state perturbation through two mechanisms before it reaches an estimator on the predictor feature. Its recurrent update averages over context, so a change in a single frame reaches the state at a fraction of its size and recovers only as the change persists. Its reconstruction objective weights an entity by the pixels it covers, so a small object can be lost due to the training objective. The JEPA has neither mechanism and passes the change through all stages to the uncertainty. We further show that this translates to gaps in five uncertainty related downstream tasks, from unfamiliar-state detection to uncertainty-penalised planning: the RSSM uncertainty misses deviations that its own posterior registers, whereas the JEPA uncertainty reports what its model sees.
ai_summary: World models predict how an environment responds to actions, so that candidate actions can be evaluated before execution . Epistemic uncertainty (EU) is the signal that marks where that experience ends .

title: What a Drop Reveals: Sim-to-Real Material Estimation for Deformable Objects from Video
abstract: How an object deforms when it hits the ground reveals what it is made of. From a single real video of a drop, we estimate a deformable object's density-normalized stiffness $E/ρ$, and its yield stress $σ_Y/ρ$ when the impact causes plastic deformation, with a feed-forward predictor trained only in simulation. Real videos carry no material labels, so such predictors are developed and validated on synthetic data alone. We show that synthetic validation ranks their geometric inputs in the wrong order. Material acts through 3D deformation, and tracklets lifted to 3D with estimated depth are indeed the most accurate input in simulation. However, on real drops they are the least accurate, and better depth does not repair them: the failure persists with simulator depth in training, LiDAR depth at test time, and exact depth on rendered replays of the real drops. Short 2D optical-flow tracklets do the opposite: they improve nothing in simulation, yet they transfer best. Material is therefore better read from what perception measures consistently in both domains than from what is most informative in simulation. Our predictor, PhysReader, reads the video and 2D tracklets and learns the lift to 3D in simulation by matching a teacher that sees exact 3D deformation. To measure transfer, we introduce PhysReader-Real: 16 everyday objects dropped five times each, with reference materials fit jointly to each object's drops and checked against tensile tests. On PhysReader-Real, PhysReader is closer to the reference materials than every other input and baseline. The one exception is a per-scene optimizer started from PhysReader's prediction, which ends slightly closer but takes 49 minutes per video instead of 12 seconds.
ai_summary: Real videos carry no material labels, so such predictors are developed and validated on synthetic data alone . We show that synthetic validation ranks their geometric inputs in the wrong order . Material acts through 3D deformation, and tracklets lifted to 3D with estimated depth are the most accurate input in simulation .

title: TIDE-Flow: Fine-Grained Temporal Evidence and Structured Displacement Matching for Spike Optical Flow
abstract: Spike cameras capture high-speed motion through an integrate-and-fire mechanism, providing fine-grained temporal observations without exposure blur. However, their binary streams encode accumulated illumination rather than instantaneous intensity, making reliable motion estimation challenging. Existing spike-based methods exploit temporal aggregation to construct motion representations, but this process may weaken fine-grained firing patterns. Meanwhile, correlation-based estimators often rely on learned matching features without explicitly characterizing the spatial distribution and ambiguity of candidate displacements. To address these challenges, we propose TIDE-Flow, a spike-based optical flow estimation framework that jointly exploits Temporal Integration Evidence (TIE) and Displacement Evidence Encoding (DEE). TIE combines raw spike patterns, multi-scale firing statistics, temporal moments, and boundary-aware interval cues, preserving complementary temporal information before spatial feature compression. DEE further integrates structured candidate-grid features with explicit displacement statistics to characterize matching geometry and competing correspondences. Both components are incorporated into a difference-correlation recurrent refinement framework, enabling effective temporal motion modeling and correspondence estimation. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of TIDE-Flow, with controlled ablations validating the contributions of temporal and displacement evidence modeling.
ai_summary: Spike cameras capture high-speed motion through an integrate-and-fire mechanism . However, their binary streams encode accumulated illumination rather than instantaneous intensity . Existing spike-based methods exploit temporal aggregation to construct motion representations . This process may weaken fine-grained firing patterns .

title: Probing Visual Idiosyncrasies in Text-to-Image Models
abstract: Text-to-Image (T2I) models turn short text descriptions into images, and the leading models now produce images of comparable visual quality. Whether their outputs still carry model-specific characteristics matters for attribution, for model comparison beyond aggregate quality, and for evaluations that assume anonymity. We ask whether images from frontier T2I models can still be classified by source, and which visual properties make this possible. Here we show that a standard ResNet-50 identifies the source of an image among HiDream-O1-Dev, FLUX.2-dev, HunyuanImage-3.0, and Qwen-Image-2512, the four highest-ranked open-source models on the Text-to-Image Arena, with 100.00% accuracy on held-out prompts. Human participants reach only 62.61% on the pairwise version of this task, so the distinguishing cues are not visually obvious. They are also not tied to a particular classifier and survive severe image corruptions and out-of-distribution prompts. We trace them to visual idiosyncrasies at three levels. Low-level texture statistics alone let a lightweight multi-layer perceptron match ResNet-50. Object layout, depth, and albedo estimated from the images each carry a source signal. Image captions reveal model-specific preferences in style and background that the prompts never specify. A one-sentence hint about these cues raises human accuracy by 9.03 percentage points. These idiosyncrasies make source classification a tool for measuring similarity between models and between real and generated images, and they caution against assuming anonymity in human preference evaluation of T2I models.
ai_summary: Text-to-Image (T2I) models turn short text descriptions into images . The leading models now produce images of comparable visual quality .

title: Shape-Aware Three-Way Merge for RDF Knowledge Graphs: The schema defines the conflict: an implementation and evaluation
abstract: Merging RDF serializations creates ordering conflicts and misses semantic ones. We describe and evaluate a three-way merge in which the schema defines a conflict: set algebra combines canonical triples, and a slot is contended only where a SHACL shape bounds its cardinality and both sides' changes cannot stand within that bound. Unbounded predicates union; contended slots go to a person. The same shapes graph validates the result. We do not claim the first three-way merge for RDF. Our contribution is an implementation in a production multi-agent store and an evaluation against a reimplementation of Quit Store's Context Merge overlap rule, which it extends rather than replaces, and six other strategies. Across five synthetic seeds, the shape-aware operator raised 33 conflicts, all true positives as judged by the same shapes that define them, with no triples lost or fabricated and no SHACL violations admitted. The context-overlap baseline, counted per slot, detected the same 33 conflicts but asked 845 questions. A replay built from recorded production incidents covers 105 human alias repairs (93 after excluding 12 chained pairs) and 939 duplicate-value incidents. It reproduces a triple-level limit: different names for one entity remain invisible (0 of 93 alias repairs detected, matching 0 of 21 synthetic cases). In a study of evolving shape contracts, merging shape declarations first handles the tested cardinality changes, while datatype evolution exposes a detector blind spot caught by post-merge validation. An oracle that reads no shapes agrees with the shipped operator on the facts and history of all 23 reachable single-slot cases. Under wrong shapes, a missing bound loses data silently and a spurious one only adds questions. The supported claim is fewer human decisions with nothing silently lost, for cardinality conflicts in one deployment, not general merge correctness.
ai_summary: Merging RDF serializations creates ordering conflicts and misses semantic ones . The shape-aware operator raised 33 conflicts, all true positives as judged by the same shapes that define them .

title: The Look-Elsewhere Effect in Searches for New Physics: from Classical Methods to Machine Learning
abstract: The look-elsewhere effect (LEE) arises when the location of an effect in parameter space is not specified in advance: scanning many locations inflates the significance of the largest excess, and the local $p$-value must be corrected into a global one. A well-established framework, rooted in the work of Davies and operationalised for particle physics by Gross and Vitells, provides this correction for scans over continuous parameters. Some aspects, however, remain unsettled. The definition of "elsewhere" is ambiguous and ranges from a single distribution to an entire experimental programme. Moreover, the analytical shortcuts of the classical framework do not carry over to searches based on machine learning (ML), which are affected by an implicit post-selection bias that depends on the model's resolution and expressiveness. This review covers the LEE in searches for new physics at colliders, from its statistical foundations to these modern challenges. We discuss the corrections for continuous scans and for multiple discrete tests, illustrated with simple numerical examples, and the interaction between ML and the LEE, which we connect to the broader literature on selective inference. We highlight open problems, including the computational cost of empirical calibration for complex models and the development of analytical shortcuts for ML test statistics, and offer recommendations for reporting discovery significance in both classical and ML-based searches in particle physics.
ai_summary: The look-elsewhere effect (LEE) arises when the location of an effect in parameter space is not specified in advance . This review covers the LEE in searches for new physics at colliders, from its statistical foundations to modern challenges .

title: Put the World Back: Timestamps Matter in Time Series Reasoning
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to time series reasoning. However, current evaluations often give models events in chronological order and already matched to the time series. This makes it unclear whether models use timestamps to connect events with observations or simply take shortcuts. To expose this ambiguity, we reformulate time series reasoning from a world-to-series projection perspective, viewing timestamps as explicit indices that connect numerical observations and external events to shared world states. We identify three structures that timestamps can make explicit: temporal causal structure, time semantics, and event-series alignment. Building on this perspective, we develop a diagnostic protocol that distinguishes timestamp-grounded reasoning from correlational shortcuts, a distinction that accuracy-based benchmarks cannot make. Controlled interventions on 310 questions from two tasks show that high accuracy can persist when timestamps are replaced by relative offsets or removed, while breaking event-series alignment induces systematic failures. When context is pre-aligned, models barely need timestamps. When order is missing, they use dates to recall world knowledge. Without dates, they rely on correlational shortcuts and rarely notice incorrect timestamps. These findings show that high accuracy on pre-aligned, ordered inputs does not establish that a model uses timestamps to synchronize observations with the world. We release our code, model outputs, and trajectory labels at https://github.com/tingrui-huang/timestamps-matter.
ai_summary: Large language models are increasingly applied to time series reasoning . But current evaluations often give models events in chronological order and already matched to the time series . This makes it unclear whether models use timestamps to connect events with observations .

title: $μ$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
abstract: Voice agents in shared spaces must satisfy interdependent multi-user requests while upholding per-user authority, privacy, and task constraints. Existing evaluations offer limited coverage when participants react throughout a session. We introduce $μ$-Bench, a benchmark for joint task completion in closed-loop, full-duplex multi-user voice interaction. Simulated participants act from isolated profiles of goals, knowledge, and permissions, adapting to the agent's speech and tool outcomes. Across 20 domains, 100 scenarios vary group size, acoustics, and follow-up demands to form 800 cases (408 tool-augmented, 392 tool-free). Joint Task Success (JTS) requires all user goals, privacy boundaries, and terminal states to hold jointly, while Pure JTS further disallows unauthorized tool calls; Attribution, Threading, and Coordination (ATC) diagnostics localize failures. Across 13 voice agents, proprietary systems peak at 62.24\% tool-free and 65.44\% tool-augmented success, while open-weight models remain below 20\%. ATC diagnostics show that open-weight models lag primarily in multi-turn attribution and threading, and controlled contrasts reveal that larger groups consistently degrade joint task success across capable systems. By coupling reactive multi-user simulation with verifiable session-level outcomes, $μ$-Bench provides a rigorous testbed for shared voice agents.
ai_summary: Voice agents in shared spaces must satisfy interdependent multi-user requests . They must uphold per-user authority, privacy, and task constraints . We introduce $μ$-Bench, a benchmark for joint task completion in closed-loop, full-duplexmulti-user interaction .

title: One Ocean, Many Tasks: A Data-Grounded Simulation Suite and Benchmark for Marine Robotics
abstract: Simulation is essential for marine robotics, yet existing platforms often trade off between visually realistic worlds, high-throughput experimentation, and ocean-condition realism grounded in real data. We present OneOcean, a data-grounded simulation suite and benchmark built around a unified spatiotemporal ocean-environment product that harmonizes bathymetry with data-driven currents and tides, with optional pollution fields for cleanup-related evaluation. On top of this environment representation, OneOcean defines a task ladder spanning navigation and station-keeping under currents, waypoint and route following, depth-profile tracking, area scanning, pipeline inspection, and multi-agent coordination, including formation transit, fish protection and patrol (herding), and surface pollution localization, containment, and cleanup. The suite supports multi-agent settings with 2-10 vehicles. Our simulator supports three to six Degrees of Freedom (DoF) and produces standardized metrics and reproducible run manifests, enabling consistent aggregation across tasks, difficulties, and scaling settings. Experiments across dataset variants and scenes systematically stress planning and control under data-grounded disturbances and reveal trade-offs among heuristic baselines, Behavior Cloning (BC), and a Large Language Model (LLM)-based planner.
ai_summary: OneOcean is a data-grounded simulation suite and benchmark built around a unified spatiotemporal ocean-environment product . It harmonizes bathymetry with data-driven currents and tides, with optional pollution fields for cleanup-related evaluation .

title: DocDUR-Net: Degradation-Aware Unified Document Image Restoration
abstract: Captured document images often suffer from diverse degradations caused by uncontrolled imaging conditions, which reduce readability and obscure fine text structures. Single-degradation restoration methods are usually trained and deployed for individual degradation types, and therefore require model selection before restoration. Unified restoration models alleviate the need to maintain multiple restoration networks by sharing one network across tasks, but representative unified document image restoration methods still depend on external task selection. This dependency limits automatic document image restoration. We propose DocDUR-Net, a degradation-aware unified restoration network that derives restoration guidance directly from the input image. It introduces a Degradation Perception Module (DPM) to extract degradation representations and predict degradation weights, and Degradation Prior-guided Adaptive Feature Fusion (DP-AFF) to combine learnable degradation priors with degradation features extracted from the input. The resulting guidance is injected into a shared restoration backbone, enabling adaptive restoration without external task selection. DocDUR-Net also supports a manual mode with explicit task selection. Experiments on document image restoration benchmarks show that DocDUR-Net achieves the best average PSNR of 29.405 dB and SSIM of 0.960 among unified methods while remaining competitive with single-degradation methods.
ai_summary: Unified restoration models alleviate the need to maintain multiple restoration networks by sharing one network across tasks . DocDUR-Net is a degradation-aware unified restoration network that derives restoration guidance directly from the input image . It introduces a Degradation Perception Module to extract degradation representations and predict degradation weights .

title: Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent: Self-Structuring Learning through Question Answering
abstract: We consider the problem of constructing knowledge bases for applications based on large language models, in which the structure of a knowledge base determines how an application can retrieve and connect the information needed to answer a question. We study Self-Structuring Learning, a setting in which questions and expected answers guide the construction of a persistent knowledge base whose editable structure can be a graph schema or the organization of linked knowledge documents. We propose Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent, which diagnoses discrepancies between expected answers and responses obtained through the current knowledge base. At each round, the method proposes a structural edit, rebuilds the knowledge base, and adopts the edit when the learning loss decreases. The retained structure is evaluated on other questions about the same sources. By randomizing over candidate edits, we express the loss change of an edit as a derivative with respect to the probability of selecting it, and we evaluate joint edits as single candidates because their changes interact. Schema Descent instantiates the method for graph schemas. In experiments on large documents, each a bundle of research papers, the updated knowledge cards and graph schemas obtain higher mean Answer F1 on held-out generated questions than their initial structures, with schema gains in every document. On human questions, mean F1 rises for schemas and falls for cards: the updated structures serve the kind of question they were learned from.
ai_summary: The method proposes a structural edit, rebuilds the knowledge base, and adopts the edit when the learning loss decreases . The retained structure is evaluated on other questions about the same sources .

title: BOP-Refer: Benchmark for Monocular 3D and 2D Object Grounding
abstract: We introduce BOP-Refer, the first benchmark for monocular 3D and 2D grounding of everyday and industrial objects sourced from 9 diverse BOP datasets. We pair images from these datasets with VLM-generated and human-verified referring expressions, and derive accurate ground-truth 3D and 2D bounding boxes of the referred objects from their 3D models and 6DoF pose annotations. Our systematic evaluation of 17 frontier VLMs across the major proprietary and open-weight families (Gemini, GPT, Claude, Qwen, Gemma) shows that the best model, Gemini 4 Carbon, reaches 72.6% AP_IoU2D in 2D but only 12.4% AP_IoU3D in 3D, despite the more lenient IoU thresholds in 3D. The predicted 3D boxes are usually centered on the target objects in the image but often off in depth by more than the object's size, suggesting that metric scale estimation, which needs reliable object size priors, is currently by far the main source of error.

title: Enhancing Maritime Domain Awareness using Latent Space Representations
abstract: This work presents a novel application of Earth Observation (EO) embeddings for Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) from the perspective of the geospatial foundation model TerraMind. By operating directly on compressed latent-space representations rather than on the original Sentinel-1 imagery, this approach directly addresses the data gravity bottleneck that increasingly constrains operational EO processing, in line with the objectives of the Embed2Scale project. In particular, linear and non-linear probing of compressed embeddings, latent space representations of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery, is used to detect, localise, and characterise vessels from Sentinel-1 GRD images. Vessel detection achieves a ROC-AUC of 0.95, while vessel localisation has a median error of around 300 m for vessels longer than 100 m, and vessel AIS type-code classification achieves 62% accuracy for the majority classes. The latter, however, is highly correlated with vessel length. These results reveal both the potential and current limitations of Geospatial Foundation Models (GeoFMs) when applied to fine-grained MDA understanding in real-world scenarios. Additionally, a new maritime remote sensing dataset is released, pairing about 2,000 Sentinel-1 images with temporally aligned AIS signals from commercial vessels. Through manual inspection, each candidate sample was verified for bounding-box quality and for consistency between the AIS-reported vessel length and the observed vessel extent, cross-checking vessel identity and location against publicly available vessel records and, where available, photographs. The dataset was made ready for use with the NeuCo-Bench neural compression benchmark framework, publicly available on HuggingFace through https://huggingface.co/datasets/embed2scale/S1-single-ship-downstream .
ai_summary: This work presents a novel application of Earth Observation (EO) embeddings for Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) This approach directly addresses the data gravity bottleneck that increasingly constrains operational EO processing, in line with the objectives of the Embed2Scale project .

title: LuxAvatar: Real-Time Relightable Head Avatars via Causal Neural Shading of 3D Intrinsic Proxies
abstract: We present LuxAvatar, a feed-forward framework for real-time head avatar animation and relighting from a single portrait. To achieve both 3D controllability and complex facial light transport, we factorize avatar synthesis into an animatable 3D intrinsic Gaussian proxy and a causal autoregressive neural shader. This proxy disentangles canonical geometry and reflectance attributes, rapidly rasterizing deformed Gaussians into view- and motion-consistent PBR buffers. Conditioned on these buffers, our neural shader formulates forward rendering as a conditional video diffusion process, bypassing explicit PBR computation to synthesize realistic shading effects under target illumination. We achieve real-time streaming through heterogeneous distillation from a pretrained multi-step bidirectional relighting teacher to a two-step causal autoregressive neural shader, inheriting broad synthetic lighting priors while minimizing conditioning and decoding latency. To further specialize these priors to human heads, we construct a hybrid relighting dataset for domain-specific fine-tuning, capturing authentic facial dynamics and physically grounded light transport. Extensive experiments show that our framework enables 3D-controllable, real-time portrait animation and relighting, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in visual fidelity, motion control, and lighting accuracy.
ai_summary: We present LuxAvatar, a feed-forward framework for real-time head animation and relighting from a single portrait . To achieve both 3D controllability and complex facial light transport, we factorize avatar synthesis into an animatable 3D intrinsic Gaussian proxy and a causal autoregressive neural shader .

title: FineDex: Bridging Fine-Grained Human-Object Interaction Generation to Dexterous Humanoid Manipulation
abstract: Dexterity is, at its core, finger-level control, yet existing dexterous manipulation and human-object interaction (HOI) generation methods rarely let one specify how an interaction is performed: five-fingered hands are often reduced to grippers, or finger usage is copied from individual human demonstrations. We present FineDex, a framework that makes finger-level intent both expressible and executable. FineDex learns coordinated human body, hand, and object motions that follow fine-grained instructions on hand selection, individual fingers, and contacts with articulated objects. To bridge generation and execution, FineDex leverages generated interactions as actionable priors for an agent that discovers physically feasible contact strategies through practice in a physics-based digital twin. By adapting at test time without per-instance retraining, FineDex generalizes across fine-grained instructions and object configurations. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art HOI generation quality and fine-grained controllability, substantial improvements in dexterous manipulation success, and successful deployment on a real dexterous humanoid robot.
ai_summary: FineDex learns coordinated human body, hand, and object motions that follow fine-grained instructions on hand selection, individual fingers, and contacts with articulated objects . FineDex leverages generated interactions as actionable priors for an agent that discovers physically feasible contact strategies .

title: Real2SimLab: A Unified Platform for Real-to-Simulation Transfer
abstract: Real-to-simulation transfer, which builds simulations from real-world observations, has long been studied in research and industry. Recently, coding agents have become capable of generating simulation programs from video recordings, and several benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate them. However, each individual benchmark defines its own inputs, deliverables, and scoring pipeline. This leads to $N \times M$ integrations when evaluating $N$ methods on $M$ benchmarks. To this end, we present Real2SimLab, a unified platform for real-to-simulation transfer. It evaluates a method by running its written program and scoring the output simulation with the original scorer of each benchmark. Moreover, Real2SimLab provides a pipeline to create training data and reward annotations for real-to-simulation methods. Our pipeline carefully avoids data contamination by filtering out the video recordings that exist in benchmarks. For each video recording, a program is first produced, and then our pipeline computes its reward with the same code that Real2SimLab uses for evaluation. So far, it supports 47 coding agents and 5 non-agent methods on 6 benchmarks. Both the platform and Awesome-Real2Sim, our research map of nearly 300 real-to-simulation papers, are open source, and we invite the Real2SimHub community to build them together.
ai_summary: Real2SimLab is a unified platform for real-to-simulation transfer . It evaluates a method by running its written program and scoring the output simulation with the original scorer of each benchmark .

title: Improving and Expanding Video Editing Capabilities Without Videos
abstract: Image editing models can follow a wide range of instructions, but video editing models still lag behind, limited in part by the difficulty of collecting paired source and edited videos. Is it possible to transfer advanced image editing capabilities to video editors without new paired videos? We introduce Image-to-Video Transfer (I2VT), which improves pretrained video editors and expands them to new editing tasks using an image editor. It enables efficient post-training with no architectural changes and no new videos, using only individual images. Our key idea is to let the video editor role-play as an image editor: it edits an image as a one-frame video, with the image editor guiding the video editor's predictions at each denoising step. Although the video editor sees only single images during training, at test time it applies the improved and expanded capabilities to whole video clips while preserving temporal consistency. To push the boundaries of video editing, we introduce OpenVE++, an extension of OpenVE-Bench that adds four new editing tasks useful for video production, including action changes, expression changes, body movements, and scene relighting. Our experiments across three different video editors show that I2VT improves existing editing capabilities and expands them to new tasks, and our models achieve state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on both OpenVE-Bench and OpenVE++.
ai_summary: Image-to-Video Transfer (I2VT) improves pretrained video editors and expands them to new editing tasks using an image editor . It enables efficient post-training with no architectural changes and no new videos .

title: High-Fidelity Image Matting with Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Diffusion models have shown strong potential for image matting by transferring generative priors learned from large-scale pretraining. However, existing approaches largely rely on latent diffusion models, whose compressed representations and VAE-based reconstruction introduce a mismatch with the high-frequency precision required for matting. We present PixelMatte, a framework that adapts pretrained pixel-space diffusion transformers for high-fidelity image matting. We show that strong image-conditioned matting capabilities can be acquired even from a pure text-to-image model without paired image-to-image pretraining. Our approach reuses the backbone's native patch embedding to jointly process the input image, trimap, and noisy alpha matte as spatially aligned tokens, enabling direct pixel-space prediction without additional condition encoders or adapters. With pixel-accurate synthetic supervision and real-image fine-tuning, PixelMatte predicts alpha mattes in a single forward pass. Two lightweight calibration modules, LayerShift and High-Pass Refiner, further improve regional opacity accuracy and boundary fidelity. Experiments across four benchmarks and two distinct pixel diffusion backbones demonstrate substantial improvements over existing methods, reducing SAD and gradient errors by 24-44% relative to RenderMatte on P3M-500-NP and AM-2K, while achieving competitive performance on AIM-500 and RenderMatte-2K. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of pixel-space generative priors for precision-sensitive image matting. Project page: https://white-yc.github.io/pixelmatte/.

title: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators
abstract: AI monitors, classifiers that flag dangerous behaviour by AI agents, are often evaluated against transcripts generated by attack policies acting as proxies for dangerous behaviour in deployment. We evaluate an ex-production OpenAI monitor as a case study and find that measured false negative rate is highly sensitive to both the method used to generate attack policies and the level of optimisation applied within that method. This rate ranged from 0.5\% to 20.8\% across optimisation levels of a single method (reinforcement learning), and from 6.4\% to 23.0\% across methods at their best observed optimisation level (optimised prompting vs.\ transcript editing). Every attack policy was developed against proxy monitors only: all reported results show attacks transferring to the held-out GPT-5.4 target monitor. Our results suggest that monitor evasion evaluations can easily mislead: an evaluation using only basic attack methods may give false confidence that a monitor is strong. The sensitivity to attack-policy choice raises a problem: interpreting any particular result as evidence about deployment performance requires justification. The transcripts produced by attack policies are proxies for the dangerous behaviour a monitor must flag in deployment. These proxies can introduce visible artefacts, such as reasoning about a ``side task'' absent from the instructions shown to the monitor, that affect monitor judgements. Given the sensitivity above, the choice of proxy can change an evaluation's conclusion. Reading these results as evidence about deployment therefore requires a separate legitimacy argument for why the proxies are informative, including any justification of conservativeness. Making convincing arguments remains an open problem.
ai_summary: Ex-production OpenAI monitors are often evaluated against transcripts generated by attack policies acting as proxies for dangerous behaviour in deployment . The sensitivity to attack-policy evaluation is highly sensitive to both the method used to generate attack policies and the level of optimisation applied within that method .

title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
abstract: Language models think in words; then multimodal models might think in images. We test whether a generated helper improves the answer to a visual question. A model describes the helper it needs and then answers using the original and generated images together. Across 13 vision-language model and generator pairs, generation lowers mean accuracy by 3.7 percentage points, with declines on nine of ten tasks. Two unified models, BAGEL and Janus-Pro-7B, each lose accuracy on eight tasks. On VSTAR, adding a generated image to the same planning hint lowers accuracy by 10.47 points. Repeated image edits yield different outcomes across tasks. ChartQAPro and MathVista stay below their no-generation baselines, while ERQA gains three points after ten edits.
